rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests a baseline multimodal setup with scgpt (RNA) and imagenet_vit_l (image) encoders, weighted fusion, and no aggregation. It clarifies whether combining modalities improves performance compared to single-modality approaches. This is the best use of the first experiment as it isolates the impact of multimodal fusion and encoder choices, which are critical design decisions.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal, singleprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, no aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves 0.422 validation accuracy. The next experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from weighted to concat (config_006) improves performance, isolating the impact of fusion strategy. This is a critical design choice with minimal other changes, providing direct insight into whether fusion method matters, balancing exploration and exploitation efficiently.

Existing evidence shows config_006 (concat fusion, ImageNet ViT-L image encoder) outperforms config_001 (weighted fusion, same image encoder). This experiment tests whether changing the image encoder to ResNet50 while keeping concat fusion (same as config_006) improves performance, isolating the impact of the image encoder. This clarifies whether the image encoder or fusion method is more critical, balancing exploration of key design choices with exploitation of the current promising direction.

Existing evidence shows config_006 (multimodal, singleprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, no aggregation, concat) has the highest accuracy (0.4348). This experiment tests whether changing to multiprofile and avgpool aggregation (while keeping RNA/image encoders and fusion type) could improve performance, isolating the impact of profile setting and aggregation. It balances exploration of key design choices with building on the best-performing configuration.

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings (config_005) achieve the highest accuracy (0.5176). This experiment tests the effect of changing aggregation from avgpool to transformer in a multiprofile setup while keeping RNA encoder (scgpt), image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), and fusion (concat) consistent. This isolates the impact of aggregation methods, a critical design choice, to determine if transformer aggregation could further improve performance.

Existing evidence shows that for multiprofile settings, aggregation methods (avgpool vs transformer) significantly impact accuracy (config_005: 0.5176 vs config_020: 0.5070). This experiment tests whether changing fusion method from concat (used in config_005) to weighted, while keeping image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), aggregation (avgpool), and profile setting (multiprofile) constant, could improve performance. This isolates the effect of fusion strategy in a high-performing multiprofile configuration, addressing uncertainty about whether weighted fusion might outperform concat in this context.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings with weighted fusion and avgpool aggregation (config_047) achieve the highest accuracy (0.542). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder (scgpt → pca_n2000) while keeping other parameters identical could improve performance, isolating the impact of RNA encoder choice. This addresses uncertainty about whether scgpt is optimal for this task and leverages the strong prior evidence from config_047 to explore a critical design decision efficiently.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile settings (e.g., config_048) outperform singleprofile ones, and weighted fusion (config_048) is effective. This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from imagenet_vit_l to resnet50 (while keeping RNA encoder as pca_n2000, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion) improves performance, isolating the impact of image encoder choice. It balances exploration of critical components with minimal changes, leveraging prior success in multiprofile configurations.

Existing evidence shows that pca_n2000 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_051) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation and concat fusion (while keeping pca_n2000/resnet50) could further improve performance, isolating the impact of aggregation and fusion methods. It balances exploitation of high-performing components with exploration of design choices critical to performance.

Existing evidence shows that pca_n2000 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion achieve high accuracy (0.6389). This experiment tests scvi_n200 RNA encoder with the same setup to isolate the impact of RNA encoder choice. It clarifies whether scvi_n200 could offer comparable performance, reducing uncertainty about encoder selection while maintaining other high-performing components.
